title: Root cause analysis: the five whys and the Ishikawa diagram

videos.script: A family paid the evening price for a morning session. The fix was one line. The cause was not. {{fix}} Root cause analysis asks why the defect was possible, so the next one like it is not. And it looks for causes in the system, never for someone to blame. Blame ends the analysis at a name. {{blame}} The five whys. Why the evening price? The time was compared as text. Why? Rafael assumed two digits. Why? Every example had two. Why? Nobody asked Célia how she types the schedule. Why? Planning never asks where an input comes from. That one, the team can fix. {{whys}} When a defect has several causes, draw a fishbone. Requirements, process, people, tools, environment, measurement. Ask each one's question. {{fishbone}} Then choose actions that change the system, give each an owner and a date, and check a month later that they worked. {{end}}
